title: Sell Mineral Rights in Fairview, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Fairview, MT
metaDescription: Fairview sits on the Montana-North Dakota line in Richland County, near real Bakken production. A retired engineer explains cross-border units before selling.
heroLead: Fairview straddles the state line closely enough that some of the mineral units touching this town cross into North Dakota, which is a wrinkle worth understanding before you sell.
intro: Richland County's eastern edge, where Fairview sits, is genuinely productive Bakken territory, benefiting both from proximity to the original Elm Coulee discovery area and from spillover activity out of the more intensively drilled McKenzie County core just across the North Dakota border. I treat this as one of the stronger positions in the Bakken MT footprint, with the caveat that cross-border units add a layer of complexity to the paperwork.

sections.heading: Cross-Border Unit Realities
paragraphs: When a spacing unit straddles the state line, the operator has to deal with two states' regulatory frameworks and, in some cases, two counties' recording requirements. If your Fairview-area interest sits in one of these units, your division order should reflect exactly how much of the unit falls in Montana versus North Dakota, and that split affects your actual net revenue interest. I always confirm this directly rather than assume a unit is entirely on one side of the line.

sections.heading: Production History Worth Checking
paragraphs: This part of Richland County has seen consistent horizontal drilling activity since the mid-2000s, targeting both the Bakken and Three Forks. Wells here often show solid early production followed by the steady decline typical of the play, and multiple wells per unit are common where operators have come back to develop the Three Forks bench separately from the original Bakken well.

sections.heading: Evaluating a Fairview-Area Interest
paragraphs: I look at how many wells are actually producing from your unit, current decline trends, and whether any part of your interest crosses into North Dakota. Given the strength of this position within the Bakken MT footprint, I'd expect a fair offer here to reflect genuinely active production rather than flank-county caution.

faqs.question: Does my mineral interest near Fairview cross into North Dakota?
faqs.answer: It's possible, given the town's position right on the state line. Your division order should specify the exact unit boundaries. If it doesn't clearly state this, a title check at the Richland County Clerk and Recorder in Sidney can confirm it.

faqs.question: Is Fairview, MT a strong area for mineral value?
faqs.answer: Relative to most of the Bakken MT footprint, yes. This part of Richland County has consistent horizontal drilling history and benefits from proximity to both Elm Coulee and the more active North Dakota core.

faqs.question: Why might there be more than one well on my unit?
faqs.answer: Operators often drill an initial Bakken well and later come back to develop the Three Forks bench beneath it as a separate well in the same unit. Each additional well can affect your calculated net revenue interest.
